design_rationale:
WORKLOG — task 0 of season_pass_billing_desk (Granite Ridge Mountain Collective, passes).

STEP 0. Draw, taken before anything was designed:
  .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/tasks/season_pass_billing_desk --tasks 2
  {"task": 0, "key": "ski_resort_operator/season_pass_billing_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 5, 6]}
  {"task": 1, "key": "ski_resort_operator/season_pass_billing_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 6]}
  This task therefore has two prerequisite problems besides the root, and the three computations carry 5, 5 and 6 factors.
  Assignment: passes_ext_arrears_recovery 5, passes_ext_reinstatement_charge 5, passes_ext_carry_forward_fee 6.

ASSET LEDGER AT CLAIM TIME. Nothing was occupied: this is the first task of the difficulty. It claims the arrears
  recovery, the restoration charge and the carry-forward fee, together with collect_past_due_0159c539,
  restore_pass_scanning_08275b43 and elect_pass_carry_forward_09e30d1a. Left free for task 1, whose draw is also two
  prerequisite problems: the credit side of the charter (passes_credit_issue and passes_credit_redeem) and the act of
  giving a pass up (passes_cancel), with passes_cancellation_refund and passes_credit_redemption as their base
  lineage — a tree of three problems that shares no policy, no tool and no base lineage with this one.

WHY IT MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one thing only: her son's pass moved to next winter. Nothing she says
  mentions money. The published terms are what tell a solver that the fee for carrying a pass forward is worked out
  only after the pass record admits the holder again; the records are what show it does not; and the restoration
  policy is what says the charge for restoring privileges is worked out only after a cleared payment stands later
  than every refusal. So the agent has to read two hops back from the request, land three writes in the order the
  sentences entail, and get three different figures right, each from a different stretch of the same ledger. No step
  is discoverable from the customer, and no tool refuses if the agent skips one.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
  Write 1 (subject passes_installment_charge, governed by passes_installment_plan):
    first_charge_lag (time). Anchor event 'the instalment plan was opened'; authoritative source passes_ledger.event_date;
    relation not_before; duration params.first_charge_lag_days = 30 calendar days; day zero is the anchor day; boundary
    inclusive. Plan opened 2026-09-12, so the earliest presentation is 2026-10-12; the handling date 2026-12-18 is 97
    days on. Negative case: a presentation on 2026-10-11 would be 29 days and refused.
    plan_open_state and stored_payment_method_on_file apply to passes_plan_open, not to this write, and so are not
    inherited here; the household does carry card_on_file in any case.
  Write 2 (subject passes_reinstate, governed by passes_arrears_suspension):
    arrears_settled_on_record (authorization, system_record): 'Privileges are restored only when the pass account
    records show every refused instalment settled.' Evidence is the collection entry the first write books, correlated
    by passes_ledger.pass_id to the pass argument. arrears_period_elapsed applies to passes_suspend and is not
    inherited on this write; it is nevertheless the clause the seed honours, the earliest unsettled refusal of
    2026-11-15 having stood the tier's 30 arrears days to 2026-12-15.
  Write 3 (subject passes_defer, governed by passes_deferral):
    within_election_period (time). Anchor event 'the pass was activated'; source passes_holdings.activated_date;
    relation not_after; duration variants.deferral_election_days = 30 for Summit Plus; day zero is the anchor day;
    boundary inclusive. Activated 2026-12-05, so the last day is 2027-01-04; the handling date is day 13. Negative
    case: an election on 2027-01-05 is out. The trap is the application date, 2026-09-08: counted from there the
    election would be 101 days out and a careless agent refuses a request the charter allows.
    no_days_taken (authorization): the account carries no scan entry at all, the son never having skied.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The object is one pass record: the Summit Plus pass registered to Kiran Raghunathan for
  2026-27 on this household, correlation key passes_holdings.pass_id. Every aggregate in the three computations is
  scoped to that pass_id. The household's other pass record, the mother's Local Pass, carries its own plan entry,
  three cleared instalments and a refusal of 2026-12-15 that was cured the next day: those rows are excluded by the
  pass reference alone, and the refusal is the near-miss a household-wide count would wrongly pick up. On the son's
  own account the second near-miss is the pair of presentations of the same instalment (2026-10-15 and 2026-10-20),
  which a reading by refusal count rather than by reconciliation double-counts, and the third is the October refusal
  that was later cleared on 2026-11-02.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
  Root: passes_ext_carry_forward_fee (the request). Prerequisites: passes_ext_reinstatement_charge, and behind it
  passes_ext_arrears_recovery. Shape: a chain of three problems, two prerequisite problems, matching the draw.
  Edge A (carry-forward waits on restoration), kind value_input, gate standing_rate, form state.
    Sentence: 'The fee for carrying a pass forward is worked out only after the pass record stands in the state in
    which it admits the holder.' Four-point test: (1) 'only after' joins this policy's own result to what it waits
    on; (2) the thing waited on is a record-visible state, the lifecycle state on the pass record; (3) no tool, no
    policy id, no code token; (4) strength 'only after' matches the edge's condition exactly. Exactly one write of
    this difficulty brings that state about: the restoration policy's own rule is the only one that puts a pass back
    into the state in which it admits the holder. Derivation: the sentence says the fee waits on the pass admitting
    the holder; the records show the pass does not; the restoration rule says privileges withdrawn are restored on
    the pass record; so the resolving action is that policy's write, and no other reading exists.
  Edge B (restoration waits on collection), kind value_input, gate expired_relief_rate, form state.
    Sentence: 'The charge for restoring scanning privileges is worked out only after the pass account carries a
    cleared payment entry dated later than every refusal standing against the pass.' Four-point test: (1) 'only
    after'; (2) a record-visible state, a cleared payment entry standing on the pass account; (3) no tool or code
    name; (4) it is as strong and as wide as the condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty books a cleared
    payment entry on a pass account: the arrears recovery. Derivation: the sentence names the state; the ledger shows
    the last cleared instalment is 2026-11-02 while refusals stand to 2026-12-15; the recovery rule is what books a
    collection against the pass account; so that write is the resolving action.
  Both edges carry a value; the floor for two prerequisite problems is one value_input edge.
  Seed evidence that each is false at the opening is recorded in prerequisite_closure.edges[].unresolved_at_frozen_time.
  Deletion sensitivity, from the Step 5 run: skipping the collection moves the restoration charge 44.10 -> 68.60;
  skipping the restoration moves the carry-forward fee 52.38 -> 44.02.

FACTOR CARD (all figures from the Step 5 run; the ladders themselves are in the charter).
  passes_ext_arrears_recovery, five factors, baseline 844.65 against gold 226.93:
    fallen_due_anchor (method) — tier taken: plan opened 2026-09-12 before the season opened 2026-11-20 and one
      instalment cleared; evidence rows: the plan entry and the cleared instalment of 2026-11-02. Baseline counts
      from the season opening and gives 0 instalments fallen due; result at baseline 58.00.
    unsettled_reconciliation (method) — five refusals in the window against three fallen due less one cleared;
      evidence: the five decline rows and the cleared instalment. Baseline takes the refusals standing, five;
      result at baseline 733.72.
    late_fee_collection (parameter) — five refusals reach the tier's tolerance of three; baseline takes no late fee;
      result at baseline 168.93.
    retry_hold_over (parameter) — most recent refusal 2026-12-15 is three days old against a five-day retry interval
      and the pass does not admit the holder; baseline holds nothing over; result at baseline 395.86.
    late_fee_gathering (method) — gathers both late fees, 58.00; baseline gathers the cycle of the handling date,
      29.00; result at baseline 197.93.
    Near-miss records: the mother's refusal of 2026-12-15 on her own pass (excluded by pass reference), the same
      instalment refused twice in October, and the October refusal later cleared.
  passes_ext_reinstatement_charge, five factors, baseline 49.00 against gold 44.10:
    charge_base_multiple (method) 98.00 vs baseline 49.00 (result 22.05); uncured_refusal_window (method) two late
    fees vs the cycle's one (result 22.05); expired_card_relief (parameter) a quarter vs none (68.60);
    unused_season_relief (parameter) a fifth vs none (63.70); standing_loyalty_relief (parameter) a tenth vs none
    (53.90). The expired-card tier rests on the three expired-card refusals of 2026-11-15, 2026-11-20 and 2026-12-15
    — the two October refusals were recorded for want of funds, so a reader who counts all five as expired still
    lands on the same tier but a reader who counts distinct instalments (two) drops a tier.
  passes_ext_carry_forward_fee, six factors, baseline 129.00 against gold 52.38:
    fee_base_basis (method) 123.86 vs 129.00 (54.34); protection_share (parameter, cross-difficulty on insure) half
    vs full (99.75); election_timing_share (parameter) nine tenths vs full (57.64); account_standing_share
    (parameter) seventeen twentieths vs full (60.74); season_elapsed_allowance (parameter) 20.00 vs none (72.38);
    schedule_carry_component (parameter) 25.00 vs none (27.38). The schedule carry component replaced a media
    component in revision 2: the media tiers turned on a serial every pass reaching this write carries, so their
    fall-through divided nobody, and the tier's replacement media fee is a charge the charter reserves for media
    that is lost, stolen or broken. The schedule carry component divides customers who reach the write by whether
    their plan is still being collected and by how much of it stands, which is a division this line of business
    genuinely draws.
    The cross-difficulty factor reads insure_holdings for this household: the Season Pass Protection Plus plan
    written over this very pass, standing with a claim open. Its rows are seeded, together with the premium charge,
    the premium payment and the cover loaded on the protection account.
    Trap: the late fees standing (58.00) are not service charges; a reader who adds them to the 44.10 restoration
    charge gets 102.10, which is past half the tier's 129.00 carry-forward fee and drops the account standing share
    to its heavy tier.
  Multi-source factors: retry_hold_over (every tier beyond the fall-through combines the age of the most recent
  refusal with the state of the pass record) and fee_base_basis (renewal source, financed state and the price
  committed to). Cross-difficulty factor: protection_share.

SEED. Every row is load-bearing. The plan entry fixes the financed amount and the scheduled instalment; the two
  October refusals and the November clearance create the reconciliation gap that separates refusals from instalments;
  the two late fees are the fee component and the uncured count; the three expired-card refusals set the expired-card
  relief and the suspension; the mother's pass and its five entries are the household near-miss; the protection plan
  and its three entries carry the cross-difficulty tier. Remove the November clearance and the recovery figure, the
  reconciliation tier and the expired-card relief all change. The account has no cache field that disagrees with its
  ledger: passes_holdings.installment_balance_usd = 902.65 is exactly the plan entry plus the two late fees less the
  cleared instalment, so no cache trap is used here. Automatic clauses checked against the seed: the retry interval
  (both retries land exactly five days after their refusal), the grace period (both late fees land after seven days,
  and the 2026-12-15 refusal's grace has not run, which is why no third late fee stands), the arrears period (30 days
  from 2026-11-15 gives the suspension of 2026-12-15) and the activation condition (the cleared instalment of
  2026-11-02 precedes the activation of 2026-12-05, the photograph being on file).

PERSONA. Priya Raghunathan, a rushed hospital pharmacist, speaks in plain words and volunteers only the surface
  request, the injury, and that her son has never skied on the pass. She gives the mobile number when asked how to
  find the household, the date of birth and postal code when asked to prove who she is, and the email as a third
  detail. Her passive branches are: agreeing when told something must be settled first and asking for it to be taken
  from the card on file; accepting a figure she is given without checking it; running the election herself when the
  agent hands it over; and closing once she is told the pass sits against next winter. She never names an amount,
  never mentions arrears or a suspension, never suggests an order of work, and never corrects the agent.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Find the household by the mobile number; verify with two details; read the pass records, the whole
  pass account and the protection plan and its entries; work out the recovery figure 226.93 and collect it; work out
  the restoration charge 44.10 on the world that collection leaves and restore privileges; then hand the election to
  the customer, who carries the pass to 2027-28 with the fee 52.38.

VERIFICATION RUN (Step 5, executed): a harness replayed the gold writes with the real tools onto this seed and
  evaluated each policy's compute on the world standing before its own write.
  passes_ext_arrears_recovery result=226.93 (plan_amount 1013.58, due_count 3, refusals_window 5, unsettled_count 2,
    fee_share 1.0, days_since_last_refusal 3, held_over_count 1, late_fees_standing 58.0, instalment_amount 168.93,
    principal_due 168.93, fee_component 58.0); factor baselines 58.0 / 733.72 / 168.93 / 395.86 / 197.93; all-baseline
    844.65.
  passes_ext_reinstatement_charge result=44.10 (expired_refusals 3, last_refusal_on 2026-12-15, last_settlement_on
    2026-12-18, expired_relief_rate 0.25, scan_count 0, days_scannable 13, unused_relief_rate 0.2,
    days_since_application 101, loyalty_relief_rate 0.1, refusals_recent 5, uncured_count 2, charge_base_usd 98.0,
    total_relief_rate 0.55); factor baselines 68.6 / 63.7 / 53.9 / 22.05 / 22.05; all-baseline 49.0.
  passes_ext_carry_forward_fee result=52.38 (protection_status claim_open, protection_rate 0.5, days_since_scannable
    13, timing_rate 0.9, service_charges_standing 44.1, standing_rate 0.85, days_since_season_open 28, season_days
    149, early_allowance_usd 20.0, financed_amount 1013.58, fee_base_usd 123.86, plan_amount_carried 1013.58,
    outstanding_share_carried 0.7102, schedule_component_usd 25.0); factor baselines 99.75 / 57.64 / 60.74 / 72.38 /
    54.34 / 27.38; all-baseline 129.0.
  Prerequisite sensitivity in the same run: restoration charge without the collection write 68.60; carry-forward fee
  without the restoration write 44.02.

TWO-WAY SWEEP rule <-> compute. Forward: every binding that reads the world or chooses is quoted in compute_basis
  against the sentence it implements, and the quotations carry the sensitive words — 'the three whole months ending on the handling date' against
  within_months=3, 'since the plan was opened' against an unwindowed sum, 'the cycle of the handling date' against
  within_months=1, 'never below zero' against MX(0, ...), 'rounded to the cent' against RND. Backward: each rule
  sentence carrying a quantity, window, branch, ordering or rounding semantic is claimed by a binding — the three
  anchor sentences by due_count, the three reconciliation sentences by unsettled_count, the hold-over sentences by
  held_over_count, the gathering sentences by late_fees_standing, the collection-share sentences by fee_share, and
  the closing sentence, which fixes that the two components are worked out separately and added once, by result. The
  same sweep was done for the restoration charge (the reliefs are added into one rate and taken once, which the
  rule states in terms and total_relief_rate implements) and for the carry-forward fee (the three shares act one
  after another, the allowance is settled against the figure they produce, the schedule carry component is added last, and
  the rounding happens once at the end).

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, the computes, the expected values and this
  worklog masked, and reading only what the published terms will carry, the tool schemas, the records the finders
  return and the caller's actual lines: the request is a carry-forward; the carry-forward rule says the fee waits on
  the pass admitting the holder; the record shows it does not; the restoration rule says the charge for restoring
  privileges waits on a cleared payment later than every refusal; the ledger shows none; so the order is collection,
  restoration, election. The figures came out 226.93, 44.10 and 52.38, the same as gold, and no second reading of
  the ordering or of any figure survived the sentences quoted above.

CLOSURE. policy -> target tool -> computation -> gold call -> terminal state:
  passes_ext_arrears_recovery -> collect_past_due_0159c539 -> computations[0] step 7 -> a passes_installment_charge
  entry of 226.93 and the balance at 675.72; passes_ext_reinstatement_charge -> restore_pass_scanning_08275b43 ->
  computations[1] step 9 -> a reinstatement fee charge of 44.10, status active, balance 719.82;
  passes_ext_carry_forward_fee -> elect_pass_carry_forward_09e30d1a -> computations[2] step 11 -> a deferral fee of
  52.38, status deferred, deferred_to_season 2027-28, balance 772.20. charter_scope, required_documents and the
  computations name the same three policies in the same order, and the three tools are the ones gold calls.


MANUAL VALUE GATES (run after the per-task scripts went green; results recorded here).
  Length and breadth: surface goal (carry the pass to next winter) -> the carry-forward rule's own sentence makes the
    fee wait on the pass admitting the holder -> the record shows it does not -> the restoration rule's own sentence
    makes its charge wait on a cleared payment later than every refusal -> the ledger shows none -> the recovery
    figure. Breadth at each hop: the tier's parameters, two stretches of ledger history (refusals in the three whole months ending on the handling date and the
    window and late fees since the plan was opened), two date spans (the plan opening and the activation date) and
    the household's protection record in another difficulty. Removing any of the three writes changes a scored
    figure or the terminal state, as the sensitivity run shows.
  Customer's own write: the carry-forward election is owner=user. The in-person semantics are the blueprint's own —
    giving up this winter on the pass disposes of the household's holding — and it completes on the spot in one call.
  Need and simulator boundary: the persona fixes the object (her son's pass), the timing (today, on this call), the
    authorisation (the desk may take what is owed from the card on file; the election is hers) and that a write is
    wanted rather than a quote. The simulator never reads policy, never orders the work and never states a figure.
  Chronology: every fact she volunteers — the injury of 22 November, that the pass was bought in September, that the
    son never skied — points at seeded rows (applied_date 2026-09-08, no scan entries). Nothing gold produces is
    known to her before the agent says it.
  Base eligibility and the time anchors: checked verbatim against the base contracts, with the boundary cases in
    solvability_contract.temporal_feasibility (first charge lag 2026-10-12 inclusive; election period 2027-01-04
    inclusive, against the 101-day trap of counting from the application).
  Authoritative facts and the business object: approval, status and settlement are all read from system rows; the
    mother's own pass and its refusal are excluded by the pass reference.
  Reachability and no real-world waits: all three writes land under one frozen_time; nothing waits on clearing, on a
    review or on a future date. Every question a real agent would ask has an answer in the persona.
  Factors, labels and baselines: each declared factor's baseline is exactly what the computation document states;
    the two method factors change how a quantity is worked out (which anchor the fallen-due count runs from, and
    whether the count is reconciled against cleared instalments) rather than swapping a number; every ladder tier
    rests on seeded rows, none on a stamp; the near-misses are present and excluded by the rules alone.


REVISION 2 (source-layer audit of 2026-09-17, report at env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/audits/policy_task/
season_pass_billing_desk/). Items closed that bear on this task:
  F0-1 / FIND-4 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED) — media_reissue_component's ladder was divided by "the pass record carries the
    serial of media already issued", which every pass reaching elect_pass_carry_forward_09e30d1a carries, since
    activation is what writes the serial and the fee waits on the record admitting the holder. The factor is gone.
    In its place the computation carries schedule_carry_component, whose tiers turn on whether the pass account shows
    an amount placed on it to be collected by instalments and on whether at least half of that amount is still to be
    collected — a division that holds of some customers reaching this write and not of others, with three reachable
    tiers and three distinct outcomes (25.00 / 12.50 / nothing). Re-run: gold 39.88 -> 52.38; the factor's baseline
    substitution gives 27.38, and the whole-baseline fall-back is unchanged at 129.00.
  F0-2 / OBS-5 — the replacement media fee is no longer charged anywhere in this policy, so the outcome the base
    rule passes_transfer_and_media reserves for lost, stolen or broken media is no longer borrowed for a
    carry-forward.
  F0-3 / OBS-6 — the four ladder value entries that named a bare share where the rule states an amount now name the
    amount ("half of the error credit standing", "half of the premium still to be collected on that plan", "half the
    tier's day use deduction", "half the excess that plan carries"). Two of those live in this task's charter
    neighbours rather than in its own three policies.
  F0-4 / OBS-7 — the two policies of this task that spoke of "the rolling review window" now say "the three whole
    months ending on the handling date", which is what within_months=3 counts. The charter's own 90-day measure is
    no longer borrowed for a window this difficulty implements differently; the tolerance the tiers compare against
    is still the tier parameter the base charter publishes. No figure moves: the earliest refusal is 2026-10-15 and
    the handling date 2026-12-18, so the count is 5 under either reading.
  F0-5 / OBS-8 — left as the auditor recorded it. unsettled_reconciliation's first two tiers state different
    methods; they coincide numerically only where no instalment has cleared, and this world has one cleared.
  Regression check after the change: steps 7 and 9 are untouched (226.93 and 44.10); the edge load-bearing run gives
  68.60 without the collection and 44.02 without the restoration; every one of the sixteen factors still moves its
  result; the terminal balance is 902.65 - 226.93 + 44.10 + 52.38 = 772.20.

REVISION 3 (re-audit of 2026-09-17, revision_2 sections of the same report). This task passes on all four
relationships in that audit; the two items it left open are both in the task file's prose, and both are closed here.
  F0-6 (observation) — evaluation_criteria[2].necessity justified the pass-record read by "the media serial the
    media component rests on", a factor revision 2 deleted. The read is still necessary for other reasons, and the
    justification now names them: the tier, the state that shows the pass does not admit the holder, the activation
    date the election period is counted from, the price committed to that the fee base rests on and the amount still
    to be collected that the schedule carry component rests on. The step's objective was trimmed in the same pass.
  F0-7 (observation) — five factor_sensitivity tier_taken strings and three prose sentences still said "the rolling
    review window" or "the rolling ninety days", wording the charter no longer contains. Every one now carries the
    reworked ladder's own words, "the three whole months ending on the handling date": the tier_taken entries for
    unsettled_reconciliation, late_fee_collection, late_fee_gathering, expired_card_relief and charge_base_multiple,
    the necessity of the pass-account read, and the two argument tracings for the presented amount and the
    restoration charge. Checked by matching each tier_taken against the when clauses of its own factor's ladder.
    No figure moves: all five refusals of 2026-10-15, 10-20, 11-15, 11-20 and 12-15 fall inside both spans.
  F0-1 to F0-5 stand as the re-audit records them: F0-1, F0-2, F0-3 and F0-4 closed, F0-5 (OBS-8) standing with
    reasons. The three scored figures are untouched by this revision — 226.93, 44.10 and 52.38 — as are both edge
    counterfactuals (68.60 without the collection, 44.02 without the restoration) and all sixteen factor baselines.
  N-4 and N-5, the charter-global observations that touch this task's two arrears policies, are recorded with
    reasons in task 1's worklog, where the charter change that raises them is described: the refusal count is taken
    over the three whole months ending on the handling date because the restricted grammar has no calendar-day
    window, and the rules now say that in their own words rather than borrowing the charter's ninety-day measure.

REVISION 4 (re-audit of 2026-09-17, revision_3 sections of the same report). This task passed all four
relationships at that revision and nothing in it changed this round. The two charter-global red lights raised
against the round-3 rework, M-1 and M-2, live in passes_ext_settlement_credit and passes_ext_credit_offset, which
are task 1's policies; this task's three policies were compared binding for binding before and after the round-4
edits and are identical. The three scored figures were re-run on the reworked charter and are unchanged at 226.93,
44.10 and 52.38, with the whole-computation baselines 844.65 / 49.00 / 129.00, the sixteen factor baselines
58.00 / 733.72 / 168.93 / 395.86 / 197.93, 68.60 / 63.70 / 53.90 / 22.05 / 22.05 and 99.75 / 57.64 / 60.74 / 72.38 /
54.34 / 27.38, and the two edge counterfactuals 68.60 and 44.02. One charter-wide sweep run this round bears on
this task's policies and found nothing to fix in them: no expression anywhere in the extended layer combines a
count of ledger entries with a quantity of days in the same arithmetic, and every result in the charter, including
this task's three, is floored at zero and within its tool's declared range — collect_past_due_0159c539's
presented_amount_usd contract was reworded from "always a positive figure" to "never negative" so that it admits
the zero an account with nothing past due would compute.

REVISION 5 (render-layer audit). This task passed all three parts of that audit — the blind runtime derivation,
the two-way scan and the dependency-form scan — and no figure of it moves in this revision. Two of its three
policies were nevertheless touched, because the audit's finding was a class rather than an instance: an RND in
compute wherever the sentence that describes the step does not say the figure is rounded.
  passes_ext_reinstatement_charge.charge_base_usd rounded the base as it was taken, while the rule says the base is
    the tier's reinstatement fee "taken once", "taken once and a half" or "taken once for each refusal left uncured"
    and rounds only "once the reduction has been taken". The roundings are gone; the base on this world is 49.00
    times two, which is exact, so the charge stays 44.10 and the factor baseline stays 22.05.
  passes_ext_carry_forward_fee.fee_base_usd is the second instance the audit named by name: compute rounded the fee
    base to 123.86 where the prose entails one tenth of 1238.58, that is 123.858, and the policy rounds "only once,
    on that final figure". The rounding is gone and the fee base is now carried exact. The fee is unchanged at
    52.38, and so are all six sensitivities (99.75 / 57.64 / 60.74 / 72.38 / 54.34 / 27.38), the whole-computation
    baseline of 129.00 and the counterfactual of 44.02, each re-derived after the change rather than assumed.
  The three factor baselines in this task's policies that rounded a tier parameter — the reinstatement fee and the
    carry-forward fee — were stripped with them; rounding a published two-decimal parameter is a no-op.
  Half-cent ties were checked by instrumenting every rounding reachable on this task: the three scored results, all
    sixteen factor-baseline substitutions, the three whole-computation baselines and both edge counterfactuals. No
    RND argument lands on a half cent, so the evaluator's half-to-even convention is never consulted here.
  The figures this task scores are therefore exactly as the render audit derived them blind from the published

user_scenario:
You are Priya Raghunathan, forty-seven, a hospital pharmacist in Golden, Colorado, and you ski with your husband and your seventeen-year-old son Kiran most winters. You are calling the Granite Ridge guest services centre on your break, so you are polite but a little rushed, and you speak plainly rather than in the collective's own vocabulary. Kiran tore a knee ligament on the twenty-second of November playing football, the surgeon has told him no skiing at all this winter, and he never once got on a lift on the pass you bought him in September. What you want is simple, and you say it in the first breath: you want his pass put onto next winter, the 2027-28 season, instead of this one, and you want that done today while you are on the phone. You are not asking about your own pass, which is fine, and you are not asking for money back.

You do not know how the collective works out anything it charges, you have never read the terms, and you do not have the pass account in front of you. When the agent asks how to find the household, you give the mobile number the collective has for you, 3035550117. If they ask you to prove who you are, you give your date of birth, 1979-04-22, and the postal code on the account, 80403; you can also give the email on the account, p.raghunathan@frontrangemail.com, if they want a third thing, and you would rather not read out card numbers over the phone. Asked which pass, you say it is Kiran's, the one for Kiran Raghunathan; you do not know any reference numbers and you say so. Asked when he was hurt you say the twenty-second of November, and asked whether he has skied at all this winter you say no, not a single day, which is the whole point.

You have told the surgeon's office to send whatever paperwork is wanted, and if the agent mentions the protection plan you took out on Kiran's pass in September you confirm you have one and that someone at the collective is already looking at a claim on it, but you say you would rather have the winter back than argue about a claim. You do not know what state the claim is in and you say so if pressed.

Whenever the agent tells you that something has to be settled or put right on the pass account before the pass can be moved to next winter, you do not argue: you say that is fine, please take whatever is owed from the card the collective holds for you, and you ask them to tell you what it comes to. If they tell you a figure, you accept it without checking it — you have no idea what it should be. If the agent instead tells you the amount is something you have to pay yourself in person, you say you would rather they took it on the account there and then. Once the agent says the account is straight and the pass record is in order, you simply say good, and ask them to go ahead with moving the pass to next winter.

When the agent hands the last step over to you and asks you to confirm the carry-forward yourself, you do it: you run what they have passed to you with the details they give you, reading back the season as 2027-28 if they ask you to confirm it. After it goes through and the agent tells you the pass now sits against next winter, you thank them warmly, say Kiran will be relieved, and end the call there. You never tell the agent what any charge ought to be, never suggest what order things should be done in, and never press them if they seem to be missing something.
